methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective chart review with substantial baseline imbalance between groups (OBCS patients were significantly younger, had larger tumours — mean 2.58 vs 1.86 cm — more T2/T3 disease, more multifocal lesions, higher N1/N2 nodal status, and shorter median follow-up of 4.64 vs 5.54 years, p<0.0001), yet the analysis relies solely on univariate t-tests, chi-square and log-rank tests with no multivariable adjustment, no propensity-score matching, and no sensitivity analyses to control for confounding by indication. No power/sample-size calculation is reported, missing data handling is described only vaguely as 'appropriately accounted for,' and multiplicity is not addressed despite many simultaneous comparisons. The shorter follow-up in the OBCS group materially undermines the non-inferiority claim for DFS, and effect sizes/CIs are not reported for the oncologic endpoints. Section 2.5 reports only standard bivariate tests, which is insufficient to support the causal-sounding conclusion of equivalent oncologic safety.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study at one Canadian center (The Ottawa Hospital, 2008–2020), which maps to Oxford LoE 2b. The question is clinically relevant to breast surgery practice and the endpoints (locoregional recurrence, positive margins, DFS, time to adjuvant therapy, surgical complications) are patient-meaningful. However, the study largely reinforces a conclusion already supported by multiple larger series and meta-analyses cited in the manuscript itself (refs 2, 3, 14, 32, 52), so it consolidates rather than changes practice, and the modest radiotherapy-timing delay (3.93 vs 3.57 months) is of unclear clinical consequence.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the appropriate checklist for this retrospective observational cohort, and the authors explicitly state adherence. The manuscript includes a flow diagram (Figure 1), REB approval number, clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, outcome definitions (major vs minor complications, DFS), and a note that there were no losses to follow-up. However, STROBE items on potential sources of bias, how missing data were handled quantitatively, how confounders were addressed, and sensitivity analyses are weak or absent; no protocol registration is reported. No data-availability or code-sharing statement is present in the provided text, and raw data/analytic code are not referenced in any repository.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is incremental and empirical rather than conceptual or methodological. The authors position the work as 'the largest-scale Canadian analysis' of OBCS, but n=307 OBCS patients is substantially smaller than prior published series (e.g., Carter et al. n=9861, Clough et al., multiple meta-analyses already cited), and the finding — that OBCS yields oncologic outcomes equivalent to lumpectomy with higher minor complication rates and a modest radiotherapy delay — closely replicates conclusions already present in refs 2, 3, 14, 32, 44, 52. No new technique, biomarker, population, or analytic framework is introduced.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with a conventional IMRaD structure, informative section headings, and tables that align numerically with the text. However, the abstract is awkwardly duplicated (an opening lay-summary paragraph followed by a conventional scientific abstract), there are typographical errors (e.g., 'p > 0.0.5' in Section 3.1, inconsistent decimal formatting), the Discussion contains repetition (the contralateral symmetry caveat is stated twice in consecutive sentences), and the lay-summary tone of the first abstract paragraph ('helping women achieve better cosmetic results') is editorial rather than scientific. Captions are referenced but Figure/Table legend content is not reproduced in text, limiting standalone interpretability.

key_strengths: Large single-institution cohort (n=1290) with 12 years of accrual and essentially no loss to follow-up through 31 December 2021
Clinically meaningful endpoints assessed in parallel: time to adjuvant therapy, positive margins, locoregional recurrence, distant metastasis, revision surgery, and DFS
Stratification of OBCS into Level I vs Level II procedures with subgroup complication and DFS analyses
Explicit STROBE adherence statement, clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, and dual independent chart abstraction with third-reviewer adjudication
key_concerns: Substantial unadjusted baseline imbalance (age, tumour size, T-stage, nodal status, multifocality, neoadjuvant exposure) with no multivariable or propensity-score analysis to control confounding by indication
DFS claim of equivalence is undermined by significantly shorter follow-up in the OBCS group (4.64 vs 5.54 years, p<0.0001) and no formal non-inferiority margin or hazard ratios with CIs
No power calculation, no multiplicity correction, no sensitivity analyses, and only vague description of missing-data handling
Novelty is limited: findings largely replicate conclusions of substantially larger prior series and meta-analyses cited in the paper
No data-availability or code-sharing statement; reproducibility posture is weak
Writing issues including a duplicated abstract (lay-summary + scientific), typographical errors (e.g., 'p > 0.0.5'), and repetition in the Discussion
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently executed but methodologically limited retrospective single-center cohort that confirms, rather than extends, established evidence that OBCS is oncologically comparable to lumpectomy. Tier 3 (mid-impact oncology/surgery journal) is the highest plausible fit, contingent on major revisions adding adjusted analyses, HRs with CIs, and a formal handling of the follow-up imbalance.
